findings: Both reports are complete and all checks pass. Full-scale composite and restoration each have zero changed channels.
All ten original PNGs inspected. The 80 percent world image slightly softens world textures, hero and world labels while HUD remains visually sharp.

Moved captures show the world and hero in the new camera framing, with HUD correctly anchored; no obvious missing layer or compositing artifact. Static captures do not establish moving-camera smoothness.
Repeat 1 improves stationary FPS 47.62 to 49.67 and mining 39.34 to 40.13; repeat 2 does not reproduce the gain: stationary 48.47 to 48.38, mining 42.66 to 41.85.
Frame-time tails vary without a consistent advantage; the implementation adds complexity and mild quality loss without repeatable material benefit.
limitations: Mac WebKit evidence does not establish physical iPhone performance.
Rejection applies to this shared-World2D 80 percent framebuffer implementation, not all possible world-rendering architectures.
next_step: Do not publish or request a phone test for this candidate; preserve the experiment and pursue a distinct evidence-backed hypothesis.
